## Source Content 

The current Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo [is the deadliest in the country’s history.](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/8/21/ebola-outbreak-growing-faster-%E2%81%A0%E2%81%A0wider-as-drc-death-toll-passes-2500-un)

With over [2,500 deaths and more than 5,000 confirmed cases,](https://www.aljazeera.com/video/newsfeed/2026/8/24/nearly-one-in-two-ebola-patients-dying-in-dr-congo-outbreak) it’s now the second largest ever worldwide. And it’s spreading at record speed. It’s even outpacing [the West Africa outbreak](https://www.who.int/emergencies/situations/ebola-outbreak-2014-2016-West-Africa) that killed more than 11,000 people between 2014 and 2016.

What do we know about why this outbreak is moving so quickly?
